items.h: Joe Milton III secures first win as Eagles starter
items.s: Joe Milton III completed 11/22 passes for 141 yards with no interceptions or touchdowns in Sunday's win over the Steelers. He also added five rushes for nine yards. Milton did just enough to end the Eagles' seven game losing streak. Milton has a much more favorable defensive matchup against the Cowboys on Thursday, but he isn't fantasy-relevant in one quarterback leagues.

items.h: Just 141 passing yards in Week 11 win
items.s: Milton completed 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards while rushing five times for seven yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers. Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass or interception through two starts. He rushed for just seven yards Sunday after notching 64 rushing yards against the Giants in his first start with the Eagles, but Milton avoided mistakes as the Eagles rode their defense and Saquon Barkley's legs to their third win of the season. Twelve of Milton's 21 passes were directed to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) in their first game together. items.h: Joe Milton III Hopes to Make the Most of Opportunity
items.s: Following a bye week, quarterback Joe Milton III will make his second start for the Philadelphia Eagles in an intrastate matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11. In his first career start against the New York Giants in Week 9, Milton completed 18 out of 34 passes (52.9%) for 169 yards, with zero touchdowns and zero interceptions. Milton added nine rushes for 64 yards (7.1 yards per carry) in the 19-11 loss to the Giants. Milton was signed to Philadelphia's roster off of the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16, just before starting quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 17. items.h: Joe Milton III to remain Eagles starter in Week 11
items.s: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni announced Joe Milton will start in Week 11 against the Steelers. Milton started in the Eagles' loss to the Giants before their bye. He'll continue to add more mobility as a rusher to go along with an inconsistent arm.

Head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed that Milton will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers, according to NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano. While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. items.h: Joe Milton III Confirmed as Week 11 Starter
items.s: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III will start his second game of the season on Sunday, according to head coach Nick Sirianni and beat reporter John Clark. Milton completed under 53% of his passes, throwing for 169 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions in his Eagles debut, a Week 9 loss to the Giants before a much-needed bye. Starter Jalen Hurts (blood clots) has been sidelined since Week 5 following the discovery of blood clots during an international trip, and the Eagles have lost all four games helmed by Milton and Tanner McKee, extending their overall losing streak to seven straight. items.h: Joe Milton III's Rushing Gives Him Week 11 Superflex Appeal
items.s: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III accounted for 64 of Philadelphia's 92 rushing yards in his first NFL start, a Week 9 loss to the New York Giants. He ran nine times, including a 24-yard scramble on third-and-eight, and added a two-point conversion on a sneak from the one-yard line. Milton is in line to start Sunday's home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers after taking over for Tanner McKee before the bye. Jalen Hurts remains on injured reserve. Rostered in three percent of Yahoo leagues, Milton is worth a Week 11 claim as a low-end QB2 in 12-team superflex leagues. items.h: Joe Milton III underwhelms as passer Sunday
items.s: Joe Milton III completed 18-of-34 passing attempts for 169 yards and rushed the ball nine times for 64 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the New York Giants. The Eagles took a chance on starting Milton on Sunday, but it didn't go very well. He failed to score a touchdown over the course of the game and led Philadelphia to just 11 points as a team, but he did lead the team with 64 rushing yards, which helped pad his fantasy total on the day. It will be hard to trust starting anyone on Philadelphia's offense for as long as Milton remains their starter.

items.h: Joe Milton III Offers Superflex Appeal
items.s: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III made his first career NFL start on Sunday and underwhelmed as a passer, going 18-of-34 (52%) for 169 yards. However, he flashed his fantasy upside on the ground, rushing nine times for 64 yards and finishing with 13.16 fantasy points. Half of his fantasy production came on the ground, and with the Eagles' bye in Week 10, Milton should have more opportunities to get reps with the starting offense and host the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11. Milton has some fantasy appeal given his rushing upside, but he needs to be more efficient as a passer if he wants to finish the season as the Eagles' starting quarterback. items.h: Throws for 169 yards, runs for 64 in start
items.s: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble. The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries.
